title: Strategic signal cartography for low-latency regions
creator: Sofia Ramos
description: Create a prioritized map (cartography) of model supply, latency risk, and procurement/time-to-provision for low-latency regions (APAC + emerging EU edge zones). Deliver an operational playbook with concrete fallback triggers and procurement lead-time SLAs so that console routing, Dedicated capacity planning, and signals for Redwood Optimize can make deterministic routing decisions during regional pressure.
objectives: Identify top 6 low-latency-sensitive regions across current customer usage and target markets
Catalog available compatible model variants per region (open weights, quantized variants, vendor-hosted endpoints) and their expected tail latency and cost characteristics
Estimate procurement and provisioning lead times for Dedicated/Private capacity in each region (including partner interpolation and spot vs reserved options)

Define deterministic fallback triggers (latency percentile, error rates, capacity shortfall) and map them to rollout actions (route to alternate model variant, expand Dedicated pool, degrade to cached tokens)
Produce a runbook that can be encoded into routing policies and Redwoods' Optimize recommendations
methodology: Survey telemetry: extract per-region 95th/99th token latency, error budgets, and traffic volumes from Console dashboards (last 90 days)
Run lightweight synthetic benchmarks across candidate model variants from model catalog (batch sizes = 1, concurrency = 50) from each target region
Interview infra/procurement partners for lead-time estimates and regional capacity constraints
Cross-reference public cloud GPU availability and partner marketplace SLAs to estimate provisioning windows
Validate fallback scenarios with a small canary (internal test app) to observe real routing behavior and failure modes
deliverables: Interactive sheet: region -> model-variant matrix with latency buckets, cost-per-token, and provisioning lead-time
Playbook PDF: fallback triggers, routing rules, procurement action matrix, and communications template for customers
PRD section: config knobs to expose canary routes / fallback thresholds in Console
acceptance_criteria: Matrix populated for at least 6 regions and 10 model-variants with measured latency buckets
Fallback triggers defined with <=2 ambiguity (clear metric threshold + action) and reviewed by Infra and Runtime teams
Procurement lead-time estimates validated by vendor/partner contacts and documented
Playbook approved by Product, Infra, and Solutions Engineering and staged for automation in routing layer

risks: Vendor-provided latency numbers differ from observed telemetry
Procurement lead-times are longer than estimated, causing false confidence in ability to scale
Playbook actions introduce customer-visible regressions during failover
Benchmarks do not capture tail behavior under mixed workloads
mitigation: Triangulate vendor claims with synthetic benchmarks and customer telemetry
Add conservative buffer to procurement lead-time estimates; identify short-term burst fallback options
Run internal canary and staged rollouts before exposing rules to customers
Include tail-focused benchmarks (99.9th percentile) and real-workload sampling in validation
success_metrics: Reduction in customer P95 latency incidents in target regions by 30% within 8 weeks of rollout
Time-to-provision (measured) within estimated window for >=80% of procurement requests
Automated routing fallbacks triggered and resolved without customer-facing errors in >=95% of tests
